items.followUp: Describe the differences between unicellular, colonial and multicellular organization, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: The definition identifies cellular organization as the way cells are arranged within an organism.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the arrangement of cells to an organism.

rubric.why: Unicellular organization is characterized by one cell carrying out life functions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one cell performs the organism’s life functions.

rubric.why: Colonial organization involves similar cells living together as a colony.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing cells living together in a colony.

rubric.why: Multicellular organization involves many cells that are specialized and work together, with division of labour.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the organism has many cells and 1 mark for stating that the cells are specialized or have a division of labour.

modelAnswer: Cellular organization is the arrangement of cells in an organism.
In unicellular organization, a single cell performs all the life functions, as in Amoeba.
In colonial organization, similar cells live together in a colony, as in Volvox.
In multicellular organization, many specialized cells work together, with a division of labour, as in plants and animals.

items.followUp: Explain how ATP is formed during respiration and how cells use the energy it provides.

rubric.why: ATP is identified as the chief energy currency or carrier in cells.
rubric.description: Identifies ATP’s role as the cell’s energy currency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ATP serves as an energy currency or carrier.

rubric.why: ATP stores usable energy in bonds between its phosphate groups.
rubric.description: Explains where energy is stored in ATP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking energy storage to ATP’s phosphate bonds.

rubric.why: ATP breakdown produces ADP and phosphate and releases energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the breakdown products and that energy is released.

rubric.why: ATP transfers energy to cell activities and can be regenerated using energy from respiration.
rubric.description: Explains the use or replenishment of ATP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing energy use in cellular activities or ATP regeneration using energy from respiration.

modelAnswer: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the chief energy currency of cells because it transfers usable energy to cellular activities.
Energy is stored in the high-energy bonds between ATP’s phosphate groups.
When ATP is hydrolysed, it forms ADP and phosphate and releases energy.
Cells use this energy for activities such as synthesis, movement and active transport; energy from respiration is used to regenerate ATP from ADP and phosphate.
